search_log: Searched “Death Comes to Pemberley P. D. James excerpt,” publisher excerpts, first chapters, and previews; opened the Penguin publisher extract and Everand English preview.
Searched “Death Comes to Pemberley third person,” “point of view,” “narrator,” and “omniscient narrator”; opened the explicit BookRags description and the Parole Rubate scholarly article.
Searched for epistolary, frame-narrative, multiple-narrator, and alternating-person structures; found no credible source describing sustained base sections in another grammatical person.
Opened the P. D. James archive, which lists an author-read extract, but its embedded audio supplied no searchable transcript and was not used as person evidence.
Opened Open Library and attempted Google Books; Open Library supplied only catalog and preview metadata, while the Google Books page did not expose usable prose.

Searched the exact first-person quote fragments and the Harriet Smith passage; results treated the first-person lines only as isolated quotations and supplied no evidence that they form controlling first-person narration.
person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating third person, often omniscient or free-indirect, with access to Elizabeth’s, Darcy’s, and other characters’ thoughts. Numerous Goodreads event passages corroborate the publisher excerpts and scholarly whole-book description. The two isolated first-person event-bucket quotations are local character utterances rather than autonomous narrative sections; several gnomic and dialogue quotations are likewise non-base. No credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person sections was found. The only remaining limitation is that the authorized prose previews cover the opening, but the whole-book scholarly and explicit POV sources resolve that scope limitation.
